If $a$ is odd and $b$ is even, $a \circ b = a - b \equiv a + b \pmod 2$.
In all other cases, $a \circ b = a + b \equiv a + b \pmod 2$.
Thus, $a \circ b$ always has the same parity as $a + b$. By induction, $R_k \equiv S_k \pmod 2$ for all $k$. 

We can represent $R_n$ as $\sum_{i=1}^n s_i a_i$, where $s_i \in \{1, -1\}$.
